articles.title: Nxled thumps PLDT, bounces back from loss
articles.summary: Nxled came out sizzling dumped defending champion PLDT, 25-19, 25-22, 25-20, to barge into the winning column of the PVL Invitational 2026 at the Smart Araneta Coliseum on Tuesday, Sept.1. Still…

blocks.text: Nxled came out sizzling dumped defending champion PLDT, 25-19, 25-22, 25-20, to barge into the winning column of the PVL Invitational 2026 at the Smart Araneta Coliseum on Tuesday, Sept.1.

Still licking their wounds from their four-set loss to the Creamline Cool Smashers less than 24 hours ago, the Chameleons took out their frustrations on the High Speed Hitters to even their win-loss record at 1-1.
MJ Phillips spearheaded the Nxled assault by pumping in eight kills and four aces to finish with 13 points, while skipper Myla Pablo took charge defensively with three blocks to chip in 12 points.
Nxled coach Ettore Guidetti said his stalwarts responded well with the defeat by playing better.
“(Today) simply confirmed we played pretty good volleyball. We’re getting better. Our defense especially worked better compared to (yesterday) and we also served much, much better today,” he said.
So impressive were the Chameleons that they only gave up 12 points on errors throughout the one hour, 30-minute match compared to the High Speed Hitters, who stumbled into 21 unforced errors.

Though PLDT held the edge in attacks, 44-41, Nxled made the most of its net defense with seven blocks. The Chameleons also capitalized on the High Speed Hitters’ shaky first ball, firing six aces to keep PLDT on the back foot.
Lyann De Guzman also paced Nxled by pouring all her 10 points on attacks, while Gel Cayuna distributed the ball well with 15 excellent sets.

Savi Davison was the lone bright spot for PLDT after erupting for 20 points, but couldn’t get the needed support as none from her teammates scored in double figures. Mika Reyes was limited to eight points, while Kianna Dy and Majoy Baron were held to just four and three points, respectively.
The High Speed Hitters fell to a 1-1card, failing to follow up their four-set win over EST Cola on Monday, Aug. 31.

articles.title: Davao to host full-distance IRONMAN race in 2027
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Sunrise Events Inc. (SEI) and the IRONMAN Group Philippines have officially unveiled the second full-distance IRONMAN race in the country, with Davao City set to host the…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Sunrise Events Inc. (SEI) and the IRONMAN Group Philippines have officially unveiled the second full-distance IRONMAN race in the country, with Davao City set to host the inaugural IRONMAN Davao on June 13, 2027.
SEI General Manager and IRONMAN Group Philippines head announced the new race earlier this week through a Facebook post.

Galura also told CDN Digital that the full-distance IRONMAN race in Davao is currently scheduled only for 2027, although organizers are already looking at the possibility of holding the event there on a long-term basis.
The move could signal the end of the full-distance IRONMAN race in Subic Bay, Zambales, although Galura declined to provide further details.
IRONMAN Davao will mark the first time the full-distance IRONMAN race will be held outside Subic Bay since 2018.

The full IRONMAN distance covers 226 kilometers, consisting of a 3.8-kilometer swim, 180-kilometer bike ride and 42.2-kilometer run. The event is expected to attract around 1,000 triathletes, similar to the shorter but equally demanding IRONMAN 70.3 Davao.
The inaugural IRONMAN Philippines in Subic drew more than 1,200 triathletes.
Still, those numbers pale in comparison with the annual participation in the IRONMAN 70.3 Lapu-Lapu, which consistently attracts more than 1,400 triathletes.

In the most recent edition on Aug. 9, 1,412 triathletes from 48 countries took part in the race. Around 10 percent failed to finish after strong currents and big waves caused by the southwest monsoon, or habagat, forced organizers to shorten the age-group swim course from 1.9 kilometers to 1 kilometer.

Despite the challenging conditions, the race was successfully completed, with 2024 champion Henri Schoeman of South Africa winning the men’s professional division and Australia’s Natalie Van Coevorden topping the women’s pro field.
SEI and the IRONMAN Group Philippines have also unveiled a new IRONMAN 70.3 race in Laoag, which will debut in 2027.
The addition of Laoag expands the country’s IRONMAN 70.3 calendar to five destinations: Lapu-Lapu, Davao, Puerto Princesa, Subic and Laoag.

articles.title: Another tornado hits Ilocos Sur, rips off roofs
articles.summary: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — A tornado tore off the roof of a house in Barangay Pudoc Norte here shortly after midnight Tuesday as tornadoes or tornado-like winds were reported in several other parts…

blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — A tornado tore off the roof of a house in Barangay Pudoc Norte here shortly after midnight Tuesday as tornadoes or tornado-like winds were reported in several other parts of the province over the past two days.
The tornado struck at about 12:10 a.m., according to initial reports. No injuries were immediately reported.
The latest incident followed tornadoes that swept through parts of Ilocos Sur on Monday afternoon, sending roofing materials and other debris flying.
In nearby Caoayan town, residents also reported another “ipo-ipo” or twister, prompting warnings for residents to remain alert.
In Bantay town, the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (MDRRMO) conducted inspections and clearing operations in areas affected by a reported tornado.

Bantay Vice Mayor Samuel G.F Parilla II said the response team assessed the affected areas, removed debris and other obstructions, and monitored conditions to ensure residents’ safety and keep roads and public areas accessible.
On Monday, strong winds swept through the municipality of Cabugao at around 5 p.m., with videos shared by residents showing roofing materials and other debris being lifted by the winds.
A similar weather event was reported in Barangay Zapat, Sinait, while strong winds damaged five beach cottages in Barangay Sulvec, Narvaca.
A video posted by the Barangay Sulvec government showed barangay officials and police officers helping clear the damaged cottages.
Authorities were continuing to assess the extent of damage in the affected communities.
No fatalities or injuries were reported from the tornado incidents, according to the latest available reports. Kenneth P. Tabin/Contributor/coa

articles.title: Thailand women’s volleyball makes Olympic history with win over China
articles.summary: BANGKOK– Thailand’s women’s national volleyball team made history after defeating hosts China 3-2 in the final of the 2026 AVC Women’s Volleyball Asian Championship, successfully defending their…

blocks.text: Thailand’s women’s national volleyball books a ticket to the LA 2028 Olympics. –THAILAND VOLLEYBALL ASSOCIATION

BANGKOK– Thailand’s women’s national volleyball team made history after defeating hosts China 3-2 in the final of the 2026 AVC Women’s Volleyball Asian Championship, successfully defending their continental title and securing their first-ever place at the Olympic Games.
The five-set victory earned Thailand direct qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, marking the first time the women’s national volleyball team will compete on the Olympic stage.

Thailand made an impressive start to the final, carrying their confidence from the previous round into a strong opening set. Solid defence combined with an effective attack allowed them to control the contest and take the first set 25-20.

China responded emphatically in the second. Thailand began to struggle with their serve reception, while the hosts found greater consistency in both attack and defence. China dominated the set 25-11 to level the match at 1-1.

Thailand regrouped in the third and produced a much tighter contest, taking the lead at stages during the middle and latter part of the set. China, however, raised their level at the decisive moments and overturned the deficit to win 25-23, moving 2-1 ahead.

Needing the fourth set to keep the match alive, Thailand responded strongly. Their attacking rhythm returned, while improved defence created opportunities to dictate play. A 25-18 victory levelled the match at 2-2 and forced a deciding fifth set.

The two teams remained locked in a tense battle in the decider amid strong support for the hosts. Thailand maintained their composure under pressure and won the decisive points to close out the set 15-10, completing a 3-2 victory.
The result secured another Asian championship for Thailand and, more significantly, delivered direct qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.
After generations of Thai players pursued the Olympic dream, Thailand’s women’s national volleyball team will now compete at the Games for the first time in its history.

articles.title: Foreign debt service burden climbs to $6.21 billion at end-May on higher principal payments
articles.summary: The Philippines ’ external debt service burden (DSB) increased by 4.8 percent to $6.21 billion in the first five months of 2026 from $5.93 billion in the same period in 2025 on the back of scheduled…

blocks.text: The Philippines ’ external debt service burden (DSB) increased by 4.8 percent to $6.21 billion in the first five months of 2026 from $5.93 billion in the same period in 2025 on the back of scheduled repayments. The latest Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) data showed that the increase in the country’s servicing of its foreign debt was fueled by a rise in principal payments, which offset a marginal decline in interest payments (IPs). An increasing external DSB indicates that a larger portion of the country’s financial resources is being used to pay off foreign obligations. Amortization, or principal payments, rose by 13.6 percent to $3.01 billion during the five-month period from $2.65 billion last year. Meanwhile, IPs edged down by 2.3 percent to $3.2 billion from $3.28 billion a year ago. SM Investment Corp. (SMIC) group economist Robert Dan Roces said the rising debt service largely reflects “scheduled repayments, not financial stress.” “More debt matured during the period, pushing principal payments higher, while IPs declined. With ample reserves and steady foreign currency inflows, the country remains well-positioned to meet its external obligations,” Roces said. As of end-March, the Philippines’ total external debt stood at $147.35 billion, a slight increase from $146.74 billion a year ago. Government debt accounted for approximately $95.66 billion, or nearly two-thirds of total, while the private sector accounted for $51.7 billion. Foreign borrowings were equivalent to 26.1 percent of the country’s annualized gross national income (GNI) as of end-March, down from 27.8 percent a year ago. Meanwhile, the ratio fell to 30 percent of annualized gross domestic product (GDP) as of end-March, compared with 31.5 percent as of end-March 2025. GNI measures the total income generated by a country’s residents, both domestically and abroad, while GDP accounts for local output. As of end-May, the DSB-to-export shipments ratio eased to 21.6 percent from 22.4 percent in the same period of 2025, while the DSB-to-current account receipts ratio remained unchanged at 8.9 percent. Furthermore, gross international reserves (GIR) stood at $103.99 billion by end-May, down from $105.18 billion a year ago. Despite the lower reserves, the annualized GIR-to-DSB ratio rose to 773.6 percent from 616.2 percent a year ago, reflecting a strengthened liquidity buffer relative to the DSB. According to the BSP, the foreign DSB represents principal and IPs. This covers payments on fixed medium- and long-term (MLT) credits, including those from the Washington-based multilateral lender International Monetary Fund (IMF) and new money facilities. It also includes IPs on fixed and revolving short-term liabilities of banks and nonbanks. However, it excludes prepayments on future maturities of foreign loans and principal payments on short-term obligations.

articles.title: PVL Invitational: Nxled bounces back by taking down PLDT
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Nxled swept defending champion PLDT, 25-19, 25-22, 25-20, to barge into the win column in the PVL Invitational Conference on Tuesday at Smart Araneta Coliseum. Licking the…

blocks.text: Nxled’s MJ Phillips tries to score against PLDT’s Mika Reyes in the PVL Invitational Conference.–PVL PHOTO
MANILA, Philippines — Nxled swept defending champion PLDT, 25-19, 25-22, 25-20, to barge into the win column in the PVL Invitational Conference on Tuesday at Smart Araneta Coliseum.
Licking the wounds of their four-set loss to Creamline less than 24 hours ago, the Chameleons found a much-needed spark from MJ Phillips and Lyann De Guzman to tie their victims at 1-1.
Phillips, a two-time Finals MVP, fired four aces, eight spikes, and a block, while De Guzman came off the bench with 10 points and nine digs.

Nxled coach Ettore Guidetti, Lyann De Guzman, and MJ Phillips after their first win in the PVL Invitational. #PVL2026 @inquirersports pic.twitter.com/ruPapYGwou — Lance Agcaoili (@LanceAgcaoilINQ) September 1, 2026
The Filipino-American middle blocker nailed three aces and connected with De Guzman’s clutch kills for an 8-0 run and a 22-16 lead.
De Guzman and Jovelyn Fernandez sent Nxled to match point, 24-19, before Leila Cruz’s attack error sealed their win.

Myla Pablo also stepped up with 12 points, highlighted by three blocks, and tallied nine digs as they continued to miss Brooke Van Sickle due to a shoulder injury. Jonah Sabete-Escamillan had nine points and 15 excellent receptions, while setter Gel Cayuna made 15 excellent sets on top of three points.

Savi Davison, coming off a 30-point performance in a victory over Thailand’s EST Cola on Monday, stayed hot with 20 points and 16 excellent receptions, but not enough to lift PLDT, which had 21 errors. Mika Reyes chipped in eight points.

articles.title: 11 Pangasinan towns placed on alert ahead of opening of two San Roque Dam gates
articles.summary: SAN MANUEL, Pangasinan — Residents in San Manuel, San Nicolas, Asingan, Tayug, Sta. Maria, Rosales, Villasis, Sto. Tomas, Alcala, Bautista and Bayambang are being urged to remain alert as the San…

blocks.text: Pangasinan Provincial Mobile Force Company personnel inspect San Roque Dam and monitor water levels as part of disaster preparedness and critical infrastructure security efforts on Tuesday. (Photo courtesy of PMFC via Liezle Inigo)

SAN MANUEL, Pangasinan — Residents in San Manuel, San Nicolas, Asingan, Tayug, Sta. Maria, Rosales, Villasis, Sto. Tomas, Alcala, Bautista and Bayambang are being urged to remain alert as the San Roque Dam prepares to open two gates beginning 8 a.m. on Sept. 2, 2026.
The National Power Corporation (NPC) said the planned gate-opening will release water at a rate of about 300 cubic meters per second (cms), equivalent to a two-meter gate opening.
As of 12 noon on Sept. 1, the dam’s water level was recorded at 283.68 meters above sea level (MASL).
The NPC said the discharge is a precautionary measure to manage the continuing rise in the dam’s water level.
Residents living near riverbanks and downstream areas are advised to closely monitor official advisories from local disaster risk reduction and management offices.

articles.title: The floods keep coming. Nepal keeps starting over
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — When the flash flood tore through the Bhotekoshi corridor on August 26, it hit a road that had already been taken once. The stretch connecting Syaphrubesi to the Rasuwagadhi border…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — When the flash flood tore through the Bhotekoshi corridor on August 26, it hit a road that had already been taken once. The stretch connecting Syaphrubesi to the Rasuwagadhi border crossing was rebuilt and reopened about a month after the July 2025 flood that destroyed the “friendship bridge” linking Nepal to China and killed at least eight people. That repair was the fast part. The rest of the valley’s reconstruction was still unfinished 13 months later when the water came back, this time carrying ice and debris from a collapse high on Langtang Lirung.

“People were starting to forget the pain of last year’s flood,” Kaisang Nurpu Tamang, chairperson of Gosaikunda Rural Municipality, told the Kathmandu Post. “Everything was becoming normal.” Tamang’s own municipal building, thirteen kilometres up the valley in Timure, is gone now too, swept away along with the rest.

The 2026 flood has killed more than 900 people in Nepal, with over 4,200 still missing. Forty-one bridges and 42 kilometres of road were gone in a single morning. Swarnim Wagle, the country’s finance minister, told Reuters the preliminary estimate to rebuild could be anywhere between $4 billion and $5 billion. Binod Chaudhary, Nepal’s only billionaire, told Bloomberg Television days earlier that rebuilding could cost $5 billion.

Both estimates are less than what the 2015 earthquake reconstruction took. It is a fair comparison, except that Nepal was still working through pieces of that earthquake recovery when the floods of 2024 arrived, killing 300 more people across the eastern lowlands. Then came Rasuwagadhi in 2025. Last week’s was the latest.

For anyone paying attention — which most Nepalis are — three consecutive years of disaster have been described in strikingly similar language. Officials called last week’s Bhotekoshi flood unprecedented. The 2025 flood was described the same way. The 2024 floods were the worst rainfall the region had recorded since 1970. At some point, one has to ask: when the same word is used every year for the same kind of event, does it still describe the event, or has it started describing our relationship to it?

I asked Nepal’s foreign minister, Shishir Khanal, whether the government sees a pattern here or is still treating each flood as its own emergency. “We should anticipate such disasters are likely to be more frequent occurrences than in the past, and be prepared for them,” he said.

blocks.caption: The 2026 flood has killed more than 900 people in Nepal, with close to 4,250 still missing.  Angad Dhakal/TKP

blocks.text: There is a useful contrast next door. Bangladesh used to be cyclone country the way Nepal is flood country now — a place where a single storm could kill on a scale that defied comprehension. The 1970 Bhola cyclone is estimated to have killed between 300,000 and 500,000 people, among the deadliest disasters of the twentieth century. Bangladesh did not stop having cyclones after that. It has been hit by dozens since, but Bangladeshis now have a system that works. They have built a national network of concrete shelters, trained tens of thousands of volunteer evacuators village by village, and tied a warning system so tightly to that structure that a storm of comparable strength now kills in the dozens.

There’s a caveat in the comparison, of course. A cyclone is a meteorological event that announces itself days out, and the people at risk live in a flat, densely settled area where they can be moved to a shelter. A glacial collapse, like the one last week, forms in a high-altitude terrain, sometimes across an international border, and arrives down a narrow valley in minutes.

Nepal’s own mountain research body has been saying something similar about the ground itself. Five months before last week’s flood, the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) published findings that ice loss across the Hindu Kush Himalaya had doubled since 2000. Of 38 glaciers it monitors, only seven meet global monitoring standards; large parts of the range, it said, remain unmonitored altogether.

“We are trying to navigate a rapidly changing future with an incomplete map,” Mohd Farooq Azam, a cryosphere specialist at ICIMOD, said at the time. “Accelerated changes in water flows and cryosphere risks could remain undetected until the impacts are severe.” ICIMOD’s director general put it even more matter-of-factly. “These aren’t blind spots becoming surprises anymore,” he said. “They are our new reality.”

Nepal’s pattern over the last three years runs the other way from Bangladesh’s. Each flood over the past few years has been met with an improvised response built largely from scratch: army units are mobilised after the fact and drone surveys are ordered once the water level has receded.

“Our primary challenge is that our initial hydrological station was swept away on the first day,” Dharmaraj Upreti, chief executive of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, told the Post on Sunday. Replacing it, he said, requires the consent of both Nepal and China — a diplomatic step now unfolding in the middle of a disaster.

blocks.caption: Each flood over the past few years has been met with an improvised response built largely from scratch: army units are mobilised after the fact, and drone surveys are ordered once the water level has receded. Photo: Courtesy of Nepali Army

blocks.text: Prime Minister Balendra Shah, five months into office, said the state has been mobilised at full capacity. He visited Nuwakot to assess the damage, which is what his predecessor did after the 2025 flood, standing in front of a different stretch of the same river. Part of what makes the pattern hard to see, let alone address, in a country like Nepal is that each flood resets the political clock. Every natural disaster is an act of geology or weather that no government could have prevented, so the response gets judged only on the speed and visibility of relief.

When the Post asked the head of NDRRMA what it had learned, Upreti had this to say: “We are reviewing helicopter deployment logistics, helipad placements, body management procedures, and the availability of body bags. We have many lessons to implement from this experience.” But these are machinery for responding faster next time, not for catching the next flood before it happens.

Tamang, the Gosaikunda chair whose rural municipality has yet to receive federal coordination since the flood, described the same sequencing problem locally. A geologist needs to survey the area to determine what ground is safe, he said, before any long-term plan can be made. “Right now, we haven’t even been able to think that far,” he said.

Minister Khanal told me that two months before the flood, he had been pressing Chinese counterparts for a bilateral framework on hydrological and meteorological data-sharing across the border. The two sides, he said on Monday, were actively exchanging communications toward a framework agreement. It was not in place as of last week.

“I was told by some scientists who know the region very well that the glacial collapse didn’t even have a name in Nepali,” Khanal said, which probably means that Nepal either didn’t know it existed or didn’t consider it an imminent threat. Since the disaster, he said, Chinese authorities have been sharing real-time information on the new lake that formed upstream — the cooperation the framework was meant to formalize before there was a lake to worry about.

That new lake, high in the mountains in Tibet and formed by the same landslide, is being labelled “extremely concerning” by global scientists. Tamang, cut off from his own municipal building, said he and his community have no idea what’s happening above them. “There’s no electricity here, the telephone network still has no signal,” he said. “So we’re quite confused about what’s happening further up.” /dl

articles.title: Sachzna Laparan introduces new boyfriend after P50-million money issue with ex
articles.summary: Actress-vlogger Sachzna Laparan appeared to have moved on as she introduced her new boyfriend on social media, months after her breakup with former partner Mark Pascual over an alleged P50-million…

blocks.text: Actress-vlogger Sachzna Laparan appeared to have moved on as she introduced her new boyfriend on social media, months after her breakup with former partner Mark Pascual over an alleged P50-million debt.

Laparan took to Facebook over the weekend to share a photo booth strip featuring her and her new boyfriend. The series of photos showed the pair posing affectionately, including shots of them kissing each other on the cheek.
“Hun,” Laparan wrote in the caption while tagging the man’s Facebook profile.
The post drew comments from her followers, with some referencing the idea of healing after a breakup.
“Anong heal heal? Wala akong sakit,” Laparan replied to one comment.
She also addressed concerns about her new relationship, joking: “Wala na po uutang sakin na jowa, wag kayo mag alala.”

blocks.caption: Facebook/Sachzna Laparan

blocks.text: Laparan’s new relationship comes after her breakup with Pascual made headlines last July. During a media interview, the actress-vlogger said that Pascual allegedly owed her and her family a total of P50 million.

Laparan claimed Pascual had invested money in cryptocurrency and stocks but incurred losses. Despite the amount involved, she said she had no plans to file a case against her ex-boyfriend or pursue repayment.

Pascual later acknowledged his financial difficulties, saying he had been gradually repaying people he owed. He claimed he lost P150 million through cryptocurrency leverage trading and maintained that he had no intention of running away from his obligations.
He also echoed Laparan’s statement that she did not have any involvement in or benefit from the investments made in his name. /edv

articles.title: Canada’s ruling Liberals sweep special elections in boost to Mark Carney
articles.summary:
Three projected victories are ‘a message’ to US that Carney ‘has the support of the Canadian people’, says one lawmaker

Canada’s ruling Liberal party has swept three special elections in a…

blocks.text: Canada’s ruling Liberal party has swept three special elections in a result that showed voters backing the prime minister, Mark Carney, after his face-off with the US president, Donald Trump.
The Canadian Press, Canada’s national news agency, projected Liberal victories in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord in Quebec, Beaches-East York in Toronto and North Vancouver-Capilano in British Columbia.

Carney said the results of Monday’s votes amounted to an endorsement of his government’s approach. “At this consequential time for Canada, voters have placed their trust in our government’s plan,” he said in a statement.

The Quebec result was the most dramatic shift. The Liberal candidate Daniel Gobeil was projected to win big in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord, a district held by the opposition Conservatives since 2018. The region is home to aluminium producers, dairy farms and other industries caught in the escalating trade war.
“This victory means we can maintain Canadian unity all across the country,” Gobeil said.
The other two seats were previously held by Liberals. In British Columbia, Carney’s former deputy chief of staff Braeden Caley won North Vancouver-Capilano.
The Liberal lawmaker Hedy Fry told the Canadian Broadcasting Corp: “The United States is getting a message tonight. Our leader has the support of the Canadian people.”

US-Canada trade talks collapsed on 21 August after the two sides failed to reach a deal, and Trump imposed 50% tariffs on roughly $20bn of Canadian goods. Canada responded with plans for tariffs on US products.

Trump has escalated his attacks on Canada since the talks failed. He signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America,” and the US Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, said on Monday that Canada had limited leverage in the dispute because the US economy was roughly 13 times larger. Trump has repeatedly talked about making Canada the 51st state.
Meanwhile, Carney has accelerated efforts to deepen economic ties with Europe and other partners.
The Liberal sweep would bring Carney’s party to 173 seats in the 343-seat House of Commons, further strengthening its position in parliament.
The special elections were called after the lawmakers who previously held the three seats resigned from parliament earlier this year.

Daniel Béland, a political science professor at McGill University, said the sweep showed Carney retaining strong support across regions, but called the Quebec result the most significant. He said the easy win in Chicoutimi-Le Fjord likely reflected, in part, the popularity in Quebec of Carney’s decision “to pull the plug on trade negotiations with the White House”.

He said the Conservative collapse there was also bad news for the party’s leader, Pierre Poilievre. The party had about 41% of the vote in last year’s federal elections, but fell to about 13% and third place on Monday. “These numbers do look bad,” Béland said.
Carney won Canada’s election last year, fuelled by public anger over Trump’s annexation threats, and he has vowed to reduce Canada’s reliance on the US.

articles.title: Whirlwinds batter 10 Ilocos Sur towns, damage homes, beach huts
articles.summary: VIGAN CITY, Ilocos Sur — Whirlwinds battered at least 10 towns in Ilocos Sur over two consecutive evenings, ripping off roofs, damaging houses and beach huts, and toppling trees as heavy rains and…

blocks.text: VIGAN CITY, Ilocos Sur — Whirlwinds battered at least 10 towns in Ilocos Sur over two consecutive evenings, ripping off roofs, damaging houses and beach huts, and toppling trees as heavy rains and strong winds brought by the enhanced southwest monsoon, or "habagat", continued to lash at the province.

Ilocos Sur Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Officer Rhon Arquelada said that, as of noon Tuesday, September 1, the affected towns were Burgos, Bantay, Narvacan, Cabugao, Sinait, Magsingal, Sto. Domingo, San Vicente, Santa Catalina, and Caoayan.
The first reported whirlwind struck Burgos on Sunday evening, August 30, while the nine other towns were hit on Monday evening, August 31.
“We are still in the process of assessing the damage to houses and huts caused by the whirlwinds in the other towns in the province,” Arquelada said.
Except for Burgos and Bantay, most of the affected areas were in coastal towns.
At least 10 houses were partially damaged after a strong whirlwind swept through Barangays Manaboc and Bangbangar in Burgos at around 6 p.m. Sunday at the height of heavy rains.
The whirlwind ripped through roofs of houses and garages and uprooted trees as powerful winds swept across the two villages.
According to the Burgos Municipal Police Station, barangay officials alerted authorities about the whirlwind while police personnel were conducting situational monitoring through handheld radios.
Police personnel and members of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office immediately responded to verify the reports and assess the damage.
Affected residents were assisted and moved to safer areas while clearing operations were conducted in the communities.
In Narvacan, four huts at WOW Sulvec Beach in Barangay Sulvec were heavily damaged after a whirlwind suddenly struck the area.
PLT Reynald Ramos of Narvacan town said some of the huts collapsed while others had their roofs blown off by the powerful winds.
Several trees in the area were also knocked down.
Authorities and concerned agencies immediately conducted clearing operations to remove debris, ensure public safety, and make the affected area passable.
In nearby Cabugao town, another whirlwind struck at around 6:30 p.m., affecting Barangays Quezon, Baclig, and Rizal.
PMajor Pol Areola of the Cabugao Municipal Police Station said authorities were still assessing the damage to houses and other properties.
Several trees were toppled onto roads, while some houses sustained partial damage.
Another whirlwind also swept through Barangay Aging in Sinait town, damaging houses and uprooting trees as strong winds battered the village.
Several houses reportedly had their roofs blown off.
Authorities were continuing damage assessments in all affected areas.
No injuries or casualties were reported in any of the whirlwind incidents.
Arquelada said the Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office remains on heightened alert as heavy rains associated with the Habagat continue to affect Ilocos Sur.
As of noon Tuesday, at least 90 families, or 225 individuals, from 18 towns in the province remained in evacuation centers for safety amid continuing heavy rains.
Meanwhile, a total of 5,026 families, or 17,371 individuals, have been affected by the continuing inclement weather in the province. (Freddie G. Lazaro)

articles.title: Red, yellow alerts up in Visayas, Mindanao grid amid power woes
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Power supply continues to be an issue in both the Visayas and Mindanao grids, prompting the issuance of red and yellow alerts anew for Tuesday. The Visayas grid is on red alert…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Power supply continues to be an issue in both the Visayas and Mindanao grids, prompting the issuance of red and yellow alerts anew for Tuesday.
The Visayas grid is on red alert from 2 p.m. until 9 p.m., and yellow alert from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m, and from 9 p.m. to 10 p.m., the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) announced.
This is because available capacity is estimated at around 2,168 megawatts (MW), well below both demand and the grid’s regulating requirements.
Capacity is limited by, among others, the forced outages of major coal-fired power plants, namely Unit 1 of Therma Visayas Inc. (TVI) and Unit 3 of Panay Energy Development Corporation (PEDC).
NGCP said supply imports from the Mindanao grid are also low.

The unavailable generating units of TVI and PEDC are among the 10 in the Visayas grid that are not working for August alone, while 20 other power plants are on forced outage as far back as five years ago.
There are also 17 other units operating at derated capacities, bringing the total capacity loss across the grid to approximately 813.9 MW.

NGCP issues a yellow alert when a grid’s operating margin is short of the contingency requirement, while a red alert is raised when supply is insufficient to meet both the consumer demand and the grid’s regulating requirement.
Relatively, the Mindanao grid is on yellow alert from 1 p.m. until 8 p.m, as available capacity is pegged to be around 2,555MW while peak demand is projected to hit 2,450MW.

Outages at major power plants are also a primary factor contributing to the low power supply. The grid operator cited the unavailability of Unit 2 of GNPower Kauswagan, as well as the forced outages of GNPK1 and Unit 2 of Therma South, Inc., as key contributors.

NGCP said 20 power plants in Mindanao were unavailable last August alone, while nine others have not been working since 2024. Six others are working at derated performance, for a total loss of around 766.3MW.

The Visayas and Mindanao grids have been experiencing forced outages during the summer due to high demand and low capacity, as some power plants are under maintenance shutdown while others are on forced outage due to several factors.
Authorities said measures are being undertaken, such as tapping battery-powered generators to boost capacity. (PNA)

articles.title: Mayon sulfur dioxide emissions surge amid signs of rising volcanic unrest
articles.summary: Mayon Volcano’s sulfur dioxide (SO2) emissions rose on Monday, Sept. 1, reaching the second-highest level recorded since volcanic gas concentrations began declining in July, said the Philippine…

blocks.text: Mayon Volcano’s sulfur dioxide (SO2) emissions rose on Monday, Sept. 1, reaching the second-highest level recorded since volcanic gas concentrations began declining in July, said the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs).
The volcano recorded 7,115 tons of SO2 emissions on Aug. 31 based on averaged measurements from stationary ultraviolet spectrometry.
Since Mayon’s alert status was lowered to Alert Level 2 on Aug. 5, its SO2 emissions had averaged only 3,844 tons per day.
The increase was accompanied by a slight rise in low-frequency volcanic earthquakes (LFVQs), which are attributed to volcanic degassing.
As of Tuesday, the Mayon Volcano Network had recorded 12 LFVQs.
However, Phivolcs said real-time seismic energy release has remained in the background levels.
The agency also noted “a short-term trend of swelling or pressurization” in the northern and eastern sectors of the volcano’s edifice based on readings from electronic tilt deformation stations.
“Elevated volcanic SO2 emissions could forewarn of a potential shift to renewed eruptive activity at the summit crater,” Phivolcs said.
It warned that renewed activity could generate volcanic hazards around Mayon, with the impacts potentially worsened by prevailing poor weather conditions.
Phivolcs reminded the public that Mayon remains at Alert Level 2, or moderate level of unrest, but said there are “new possibilities of eruptive unrest recurring.”

The agency warned that a new phase of eruption could generate life-threatening volcanic hazards, including pyroclastic density currents (PDCs) or uson, rockfall, ballistic fragments that can be thrown from the crater, and extensive ashfall that could severely affect communities downwind of the volcano.

Phivolcs reminded the public to refrain from entering the six-kilometer radius permanent danger zone and urged communities and local government units within predetermined PDC hazard zones to prepare for a possible escalation to Alert Level 3.

It also called for increased vigilance and pre-emptive response actions against lahars and sediment-laden streamflow along channels draining Mayon during sustained heavy or intense rains, especially if an explosive eruption occurs simultaneously.

Civil aviation authorities were also advised to continue telling pilots to avoid flying close to Mayon’s summit, as ash and ballistic fragments from any sudden eruption could pose hazards to aircraft.

articles.title: Face masks distributed in Mamburao schools amid Mindoro haze
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro. — The municipal government of Mamburao has ordered the distribution of face masks to schools as a precaution against haze observed in parts of Occidental Mindoro.…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro. — The municipal government of Mamburao has ordered the distribution of face masks to schools as a precaution against haze observed in parts of Occidental Mindoro.
Mamburao Mayor Glicerio Almero III said local government personnel were tasked to distribute face masks to schools, with the supplies to be turned over to school heads.
“Ibibigay po natin sa mga school heads and priority po yung may mga kondisyon sa lungs and heart,” Almero said.
(We will task school heads to determine their priority to be given face masks, preferably to those with lung and heart conditions)
The move came as local authorities in Mindoro advised residents to take precautions amid the spread of haze, which is believed to be linked to smoke from forest fires in Indonesia.

In a separate public advisory issued on Sept. 1, the Calapan City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office urged residents to remain vigilant over the haze, which may be caused by smoke from forest and land fires in Indonesia, particularly in Sumatra and Kalimantan, that winds carried to other parts of Southeast Asia.
The public was advised to wear face masks when going outdoors and avoid staying for prolonged periods in areas where haze or smoke is noticeable.
Residents were also urged to monitor official air quality advisories and take appropriate precautions.
Children, older adults and people with existing lung or heart conditions are considered particularly vulnerable and were advised to take extra care./coa

articles.title: UAAP adjusts September basketball schedule for Gilas duties
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The UAAP is adjusting its September basketball schedule to accommodate the Gilas Pilipinas’ campaigns in the Asian Games and Fiba 3×3 Under-23 World Cup. There will…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The UAAP is adjusting its September basketball schedule to accommodate the Gilas Pilipinas’ campaigns in the Asian Games and Fiba 3×3 Under-23 World Cup.
There will be only five gamedays for the collegiate men’s and women’s basketball tournaments from Sept. 13 to 30, the UAAP announced.
The Season 89 opening ceremony is set for Sept. 12 at Mall of Asia Arena, with the first men’s basketball games scheduled the following day at the Smart Araneta Coliseum.

Far Eastern University will face Adamson at noon, followed by defending champion La Salle against National University at 2:30 p.m. University of the Philippines will then take on University of Santo Tomas at 6 p.m.
The men’s schedule will continue on September 16 at MOA Arena, September 19 at Smart Araneta Coliseum, September 26 at MOA Asia Arena and September 30 at the same venue.
The schedule adjustments were made as several UAAP players are set to represent the Philippines in September.

“We have always believed that the UAAP’s mission goes beyond the competition. We are here to develop student-athletes who can represent our schools, but we are equally proud when they get the opportunity to represent the country,” said UAAP Season 89 President Mark Molina of Far Eastern University. FEU’s Cabs Cabonilas and Jedric Daa and Adamson’s Earl Medina are scheduled to compete in the Fiba 3×3 Under-23 World Cup in Wuhan, China, from September 15 to 19.
La Salle’s Luis Pablo and Doy Dungo and UST’s Koji Buenaflor are set to suit up for Gilas Pilipinas 3×3 in the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, from September 21 to 25.
The collegiate women’s basketball tournament will also start later as the national teams for the Asian Games and the U23 World Cup are expected to include several UAAP student-athletes.

“The support of the UAAP is important to our national team programs, especially with so many of our student-athletes being called up to represent the country,” Samahang Basketbol ng Pilipinas Executive Director Erika Dy said.
“We appreciate the UAAP for working closely with us and for making the necessary adjustments to accommodate our national team commitments.”

articles.title: Putin-Modi meeting at SCO: Can Russia-India ties hold?
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to meet in Kyrgyzstan’s capital, Bishkek, on Monday on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization…

blocks.text: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin are set to meet in Kyrgyzstan’s capital, Bishkek, on Monday on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit — a bloc often seen as a counterweight to US influence.
The meeting comes against the backdrop of the fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran, which has disrupted global energy markets, and Russia’s war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year.
India has remained engaged with the SCO while resisting efforts to turn it into an anti-Western bloc. Its position reflects a broader effort to maintain relationships with competing powers.

That approach is under greater pressure. Russia remains under Western sanctions over the war in Ukraine. Meanwhile, India has faced US pressure over its purchases of Russian oil, alongside wider trade tensions.
A former Indian ambassador to the US, Meera Shankar, told DW that India’s relationship with Russia should not be seen as directed against the US.
“India has a long-standing strategic relationship with Russia. This is not directed against any country but intended to help India meet its national goals,” said Shankar.
Energy ties deepen between India, Russia
Energy has become the most visible change in the India-Russia relationship.

Before 2022, when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, it supplied only a small share of India’s crude imports. Discounted Russian oil rapidly changed that, making Moscow one of India’s biggest suppliers.

It has also become the most contentious part of India’s relationship with the US, which has pressed New Delhi to reduce its purchases from Russia. India maintains that securing affordable and reliable energy is a national interest.

The disruption to traditional energy supplies has made that calculation more complicated. This year’s US-Israel war on Iran and disruption of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz have affected India’s purchases from the Gulf and pushed up prices.
Shankar said India is responding by diversifying its sources of supply, including both Russia and the US.
“In the long run, a transition to a non-fossil fuel economy would strengthen India’s energy independence. But this will not happen overnight,” she added.
Until then, Shankar said, India will take steps it considers necessary to stabilize supplies and protect its people.
Future of India-Russia defense cooperation
Defense remains the other major pillar, but here the direction of travel is clearer: India’s dependence on Russian equipment has been declining.
The Ukraine war has raised questions over Russia’s production capacity, delivery schedules and ability to supply spare parts after decades as a major supplier of India’s military hardware.

“India remains one of Russia’s oldest and largest arms buyers, and perhaps the last major one,” Aravind Yelery, an associate professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in the Indian capital, New Delhi, told DW.

“New Delhi is increasingly reluctant to commit to Russia’s fifth-generation fighter program and has little appetite for new Russian hardware unless it can be incorporated into India’s indigenous production plans,” he added.
While India has diversified its purchases, that does not mean the defense relationship is disappearing.
However, the terms are changing, with India looking for a relationship that contributes to its own defense production, so that it can move away from simply buying finished systems.
The China question
Russia’s growing dependence on China has also become an unavoidable part of the India-Russia equation.

Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in early 2022, China has become indispensable to Russia as a market, supplier and economic partner. That has reduced Moscow’s ability to serve as a counterweight to Beijing.
Yelery sees an important distinction in the two relationships.
“Strategically, Russia’s relationship with China remains structurally transactional, a dependence it can ill afford to compromise, whereas its relationship with India rests on partnership,” he said.
India still has reasons to keep Moscow close: energy, defense, access to the Russian market and a longstanding political relationship across Eurasia. But the strategic calculation has changed.
India’s ‘America plus’ strategy
Strategic affairs expert C Raja Mohan said that Russia’s growing dependence on China has changed its strategic value for India.
“Russia is no longer in a position to help India balance China,” Mohan, a professor of American studies at Jindal Global University, told DW.
This changes India’s expectations from the relationship with Russia.

The emphasis is increasingly on specific interests — energy security, defense supplies, trade and access to technology — while India’s larger strategic weight increasingly rests on relationships with the US and its allies.
India has expanded defense and technology cooperation with Washington, while deepening ties with partners such as France and Israel.
Mohan describes this approach as an “America plus” strategy, whereby India maintains its partnership with the US while widening its engagement with other major powers.
“India is trying to reduce its exposure to American volatility, but it still recognizes that Washington is its most important partner,” he said.
What do Modi and Putin want?
Rajan Kumar, a professor of Russian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, said Putin wants reassurance that India will remain engaged with Moscow despite pressure from Washington.
“President Putin needs an assurance from Prime Minister Modi that India will not ditch Russia when the latter is facing the worst possible crisis after the 1990s,” Kumar told DW.
He expects continuity rather than a dramatic reset. “I think it is more about continuation of existing ties amid US pressure,” he added.

Energy trade and payment mechanisms, ways to increase Indian exports to Russia, defense cooperation and the two countries’ assessments of the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran are likely to remain important.
The bigger test will come in Delhi in September, when Putin is expected to return for the BRICS summit.
The Bishkek meeting can keep the political relationship on track, but the Delhi talks will show whether that political continuity can produce progress on trade, energy, defense and technology.

The relationship is no longer what it was before the Ukraine war. Energy has become far more important, India’s defense dependence is being recalibrated, and Russia’s closeness to China has altered the strategic equation.

“The relationship has a value that goes beyond individual deals. Putin appears well aware that India carries an independent strategic weight that China’s structural leverage cannot substitute,” said Yelery. /dl

articles.title: How young Cameroonians end up fighting in Russia’s war
articles.summary: Cameroon has emerged as one of the leading sources of African recruits for the Russian military, with young men lured to Europe by false promises of jobs and fast-tracked Russian citizenship, only to…

blocks.text: Cameroon has emerged as one of the leading sources of African recruits for the Russian military, with young men lured to Europe by false promises of jobs and fast-tracked Russian citizenship, only to find themselves on the front lines of the war in Ukraine.

As of May this year, Ukrainian officials say that nearly 3,000 citizens from various African countries were known to have fought — or to still be fighting — for Russia : Cameroon, Ghana, Egypt, Kenya and Uganda were identified as significant.
In April, the Cameroonian government confirmed that Russia had reported the deaths of 16 Cameroonian nationals, seven of whom had died in military action in Ukraine.

blocks.caption: Charles Ojiambo Mutoka, 72, shows a picture of his son Oscar, who he learned was killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine Image: Tony Karumba/AFP

blocks.text: Poverty driving youths into Russia’s duplicitous schemes
The actual death toll is likely higher according to DW correspondent Dorcas Ekupe, reporting from Bamenda in northwestern Cameroon.

“When you look at other publications and see what is happening — even seeing families who are grieving their loved ones — the number is really much higher than what the government had earlier said,” Ekupe told DW’s AfricaLink program.
She described two forces causing this worrying phenomenon: economic desperation and deliberate deception.
Many recruits, she said, travelled to Russia believing they had secured jobs in construction or as security guards, or that they were participating in study programs.
“Once in Russia, they then end up on the battlefield,” Ekupe said.
Russia’s perceived appeal meanwhile is also being amplified by well-organized campaigns.

Banjo Herman, a lecturer and political analyst at the University of Bamenda, pointed to the key role of the the Russian paramilitary Wagner Group as well as its successor, the Africa Corps, as Moscow’s primary instrument for expanding its presence and reputation across Africa.
Military recruitment dressed up as ‘cultural’ outreach

Herman also cited Russian government programs such as the African Initiative and Alabuga, which present themselves as cultural or educational exchange schemes but have been linked to military recruitment.

“On the surface, sometimes it looks like cultural outreach,” he said. “Sometimes Cameroonians are lured, thinking it is for work, not necessarily knowing what is beneath the surfac.,” He added that offers of Russian nationality within six months were a particularly powerful draw.
France has previously described the African Initiative as a front administered by Russian intelligence services, designed to spread propaganda.
Why young men continue to risk their lives
Herman stressed, however, that the economic situation of the men was typically the main motivator.

“Imagine that you are a carpenter in Cameroon who cannot even earn 100,000 CFA francs (€150; $175) a month, but somebody is promising you 3 million CFA francs to come and work,” he explained. “It is very attractive.”

He also highlighted the fact that not all Cameroonians in Russia were the victims of deception: Some had lived there for years, had been absorbed into the military over time and were doing reasonably well.

But he pointed out that it was the promise of financial reward combined with the prospect of gaining Russian citizenship that explained why even people aware of the risks continued to accept recruitment offers to fight in Ukraine.
Ekupe corroborated this, noting a prevailing attitude of fatalism among some youth: “Sometimes people say, ‘If I die, I die.'”
Those left behind often suffer the most

Families left behind, meanwhile, are forced to bear the cost in silence: Ekupe described cases in which mothers only learned of their sons’ deaths years after the fact — in one instance, when a fellow soldier called home to report that a 35-year-old Cameroonian had been killed in combat.
She added that many families had received no financial compensation from the Cameroonian government and that some of the men who died had left behind pregnant wives as well as children.
Contact between recruits and their families is often severed abruptly, Ekupe said.

“When they get there and discover it was not as promised, it is really difficult to inform their family,” she added. “Sometimes they have to take time to adjust to the new environment and the situation, in which they find themselves.”

blocks.caption: According to the Kenyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, more than 200 Kenyan nationals had crossed into Russia by January 2026, but only 18 had returned Image: Minako Sasako/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia ducking from responsibilty
On the question of legal responsibility, Herman noted that international law does not, in principle, prohibit a foreign national from voluntarily enlisting in another state’s armed forces.
Legal liability arises, however, when recruitment involves fraud, coercion, trafficking or mercenary activity.

Herman cited Article 47 of the Additional Protocol to the Geneva Conventions, which defines a mercenary as someone who agrees to take direct part in hostilities with private financial gain as their main motivation.
Under current frameworks, the responsibility for the death of a foreign fighter in another country’s war rests largely with the individual and their family, not the recruiting state.
Cameroon: insufficient campaigns to fight recruitement
Cameroon’s government has stated publicly that it does not deploy troops abroad outside international mandates, and has warned citizens against joining foreign conflicts.
Analysts have nevertheless called on the Cameroonian government, and African governments more broadly, to pursue a three-pronged response to stop more people from risking their lives in Russia.

This approach would include economic reforms to create opportunities and reduce the conditions that make deceptive recruitment attractive; direct diplomatic engagement with Russia to hold recruitment networks accountable; and a public awareness campaign that issues clear, proactive public warnings to citizens about the dangers of following such schemes.

blocks.caption: Relatives of Kenyan nationals conscripted by the Russian army have demanded government action to repatriate their kin Image: Tony Karumba/AFP

blocks.text: Ghana has also formally raised the issue with Russia, demanding an end to the recruitment of its nationals.
However, in Cameroon’s case, the country’s longstanding military ties with Russia, which President Paul Biya moved to renew in 2014 and 2015, could prevent a similar move.

Herman said that the absence of an official Cameroonian policy response to date reflected, at least in part, the government’s awareness that the recruitment is carried out by private actors — limiting the state’s formal grounds and opportunities for intervention.

“For the government to stop this,” he said, “it has to go back to its governance policy and have a policy that is inclusive, transparent, and in which people can find opportunities within the system.” /dl

articles.title: China-Nepal flood toll tops 1,000 as tunnel rescue offers last hope
articles.summary: NUWAKOT, Nepal — The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared…

blocks.text: NUWAKOT, Nepal — The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels.

Nearly 4,500 people are missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks and debris from a high-altitude glacial collapse roared downstream on Wednesday, wiping out entire settlements and gouging a path of destruction through Nepal.
Nepali rescue teams are digging, drilling and blasting through debris in a race against time in treacherous conditions to free around 100 hydropower workers believed trapped in multiple tunnels.
So far, only corpses have been pulled out of tunnels blocked with sludge.
“We are focused on search and rescue efforts at the tunnels, our work is continuing,” Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal Army spokesman, told AFP on Tuesday.
“Our soldiers are also deployed to collect bodies and prevent the spread of disease.”

With mortuaries overflowing in Nepal, the authorities have begun burying hundreds of unidentified bodies after DNA sampling. At least 17 bodies have also been pulled from rivers far downstream in India.
Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called the catastrophe “unimaginable and heartbreaking”.
‘Find their bodies’
In the capital Kathmandu, crowds lined up to search for their missing relatives, posting photographs on a long wall outside a hospital, in the fading hope of finding them alive.

Debu Sapkota, a 58-year-old driver, came to post photos of his 83-year-old mother-in-law and granddaughter who went missing in the town of Trishuli Bazaar, after being swept away by last week’s surge.
A warning alert sounded, but the elderly woman was “too old to run”, he recounts.
“Her granddaughter was helping her escape but both were swept away.”
Sapkota says he no longer has “any hope that they survived”, after witnesses saw them being carried away by the torrent.
“I am here hoping to find their bodies,” he said, holding up photos of the two missing women dressed in traditional clothes.
In Chitwan district, mourning relatives cremated some of the dead.
Soldiers were seen unloading bodies of victims from helicopters in Nepal’s Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts.
Aid needs are enormous. Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless and using makeshift shelters as heavy rain lashes down.
Roads and dozens of bridges have been smashed, and power plants destroyed.
“There are too many challenges,” said police officer E. Hawadi in badly affected Nuwakot district.
‘Climate change’

In Nuwakot, AFP photographers on Tuesday saw people scouring through mud into the rubble of their homes for usable items, some clearing away dirt and stringing up plastic sheeting for shelter in the ruins.
Foreigners missing among the list include 583 in Nepal and 261 in China, coming more than 30 nations.
They include tourists who had come for trekking in the apparently serene Himalayas, as well as Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.

There is growing anger at the scale of destruction to hit Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people — that has contributed little to the emissions driving global warming churned out by wealthy and industrialised nations, but is suffering its consequences.

“It is now time for us to strongly raise with the international community the issue of the disasters we are experiencing as a result of climate change,” Shah, Nepal’s prime minister, said in a statement late Monday.
Scientists say the Himalayas, the world’s highest mountain range, are melting faster as global temperatures rise.

blocks.caption: This screen grab from a handout video footage released by Nepal’s Prime Minister Secretariat on August 31, 2026 via AFPTV shows Nepali soldiers conducting an operation inside a tunnel to rescue workers after flash floods at Rasuwagadhi Hydropower Project site in Rasuwa district. Agence France-Presse

blocks.text: Nepal’s economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale, with Kathmandu warning reconstruction costs could run into the “billions of dollars”.

articles.title: After Nepal disaster, Cebu City watches Lusaran River, flood-prone areas
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Following the deadly flash floods in Nepal, disaster officials here are keeping a close watch on the Lusaran River and other flood-prone areas. Councilor Dave Tumulak, head…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Following the deadly flash floods in Nepal, disaster officials here are keeping a close watch on the Lusaran River and other flood-prone areas.

Councilor Dave Tumulak, head of the Cebu City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (CCDRRMC), said on Tuesday that authorities continue to remind communities living near waterways to move to safer areas, particularly when heavy rainfall threatens to swell rivers.
Lusaran River shows risk
Tumulak identified the Lusaran River as a key area of concern.
He said the risk becomes particularly serious during heavy downpours, citing the flooding that struck Cebu City during Typhoon Tino in November 2025.
“Kining Lusaran [River] mao ni delikado, kay same atong nahitabo sa [bagyong] Tino nga heavy downpour nga nag flash flood gyud sila didto,” he said.
(The Lusaran River is particularly dangerous because it could mirror what happened during Tropical Storm Tino, where heavy rainfall triggered severe flash floods in the area.)
Tumulak said the situation along the river has since changed, with residents reportedly leaving riverbanks after experiencing the devastation caused by the storm.

“Ang Lusaran, katong pagkatapusan sa Tino, nahawan na man gyud tong sapa. Wala na gyud nagpuyo kay na-trauma na gyod ang mga tawo,” he said. (In Lusaran, by the end of Tino, the river channel had already cleared. No one was living there anymore because the people had been traumatized by what happened.)
Still, Tumulak said the CCDRRMC would continue monitoring the area, with a possible inspection planned this week.
Clearing efforts
Meanwhile, the disaster head said the city continues its information campaign and clearing efforts involving the legally required 3-meter easement along waterways.
“Ongoing na atong information dissemination sa clearing sa 3-meter easement,” he said. (Our information dissemination on the clearing of the 3-meter easement is ongoing.)

Tumulak said the city has also begun compiling a list of families who could need relocation as authorities clear areas along waterways. The city plans to relocate affected families to safer locations rather than leave them exposed to flooding along rivers and waterways.
The concern over Lusaran comes from its experience with Tino, which brought extreme rainfall to Cebu City on November 3 to 4, 2025.
Tino dumped 183 millimeters of rain on Cebu City within 24 hours, exceeding the city’s normal November rainfall average of 131 millimeters.
The resulting overflow of the Lusaran River triggered powerful flash floods in Barangay Lusaran and nearby communities.

articles.title: China-Nepal flood toll tops 1,000 as tunnel rescue offers last hope
articles.summary: NUWAKOT, Nepal — The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared…

blocks.text: NUWAKOT, Nepal — The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels.

Nearly 4,500 people are missing after the gigantic wave of freezing water, rocks and debris from a high-altitude glacial collapse roared downstream on Wednesday, wiping out entire settlements and gouging a path of destruction through Nepal.
Nepali rescue teams are digging, drilling and blasting through debris in a race against time in treacherous conditions to free around 100 hydropower workers believed trapped in multiple tunnels.
So far, only corpses have been pulled out of tunnels blocked with sludge.
“We are focused on search and rescue efforts at the tunnels, our work is continuing,” Raja Ram Basnet, Nepal Army spokesman, told AFP on Tuesday.
“Our soldiers are also deployed to collect bodies and prevent the spread of disease.”

With mortuaries overflowing in Nepal, the authorities have begun burying hundreds of unidentified bodies after DNA sampling. At least 17 bodies have also been pulled from rivers far downstream in India.
Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah has called the catastrophe “unimaginable and heartbreaking”.
‘Find their bodies’
In the capital Kathmandu, crowds lined up to search for their missing relatives, posting photographs on a long wall outside a hospital, in the fading hope of finding them alive.

Debu Sapkota, a 58-year-old driver, came to post photos of his 83-year-old mother-in-law and granddaughter who went missing in the town of Trishuli Bazaar, after being swept away by last week’s surge.
A warning alert sounded, but the elderly woman was “too old to run”, he recounts.
“Her granddaughter was helping her escape but both were swept away.”
Sapkota says he no longer has “any hope that they survived”, after witnesses saw them being carried away by the torrent.
“I am here hoping to find their bodies,” he said, holding up photos of the two missing women dressed in traditional clothes.
In Chitwan district, mourning relatives cremated some of the dead.
Soldiers were seen unloading bodies of victims from helicopters in Nepal’s Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts.
Aid needs are enormous. Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless and using makeshift shelters as heavy rain lashes down.
Roads and dozens of bridges have been smashed, and power plants destroyed.
“There are too many challenges,” said police officer E. Hawadi in badly affected Nuwakot district.
‘Climate change’

In Nuwakot, AFP photographers on Tuesday saw people scouring through mud into the rubble of their homes for usable items, some clearing away dirt and stringing up plastic sheeting for shelter in the ruins.
Foreigners missing among the list include 583 in Nepal and 261 in China, coming more than 30 nations.
They include tourists who had come for trekking in the apparently serene Himalayas, as well as Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.

There is growing anger at the scale of destruction to hit Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people — that has contributed little to the emissions driving global warming churned out by wealthy and industrialised nations, but is suffering its consequences.

“It is now time for us to strongly raise with the international community the issue of the disasters we are experiencing as a result of climate change,” Shah, Nepal’s prime minister, said in a statement late Monday.
Scientists say the Himalayas, the world’s highest mountain range, are melting faster as global temperatures rise.

articles.title: Shein shares slide on fast-fashion retailer’s stock market debut
articles.summary:
Hong Kong flotation at $26bn by firm once valued at $100bn follows failure to list in US and UK

Shares in the fast-fashion brand Shein slumped by as much as 10% as the China-founded company…

blocks.text: Shares in the fast-fashion brand Shein slumped as much as 10% as the China-founded company made its long-anticipated trading debut on the Hong Kong stock exchange.
The Singapore-headquartered company, once valued at almost $100bn (£74bn), went public on Tuesday pricing shares at HK$48.56, valuing the business at just over $26bn.

However, minutes after the flotation, which raised HK$13.6bn, the stock fell as much as 10%, pushing the online retailer’s valuation below $25bn. Shein’s share price recovered some ground to be 4% below its offer price by the end of trading, at HK$46.62.
“Let global consumers enjoy the sound of fashion,” said Leigh Gui, Shein’s chief financial officer, after a gong was struck to mark the start of trading.

The lacklustre launch as a publicly listed company comes after one of the longest-awaited initial public offerings in recent years, after plans to list in New York were blocked by regulators over forced labour concerns.
Shein also considered a £50bn flotation in London but faced similar questions about its supply chain from campaigners, MPs and investors.

The plunge in value has been driven by regulatory changes around the world that threaten its business model of shipping goods in small packages out of China to take advantage of tax breaks on low-value imported goods.

Shein swung to a loss of $99m in the first three months of this year, compared with a net income of $395m the year before, after the US removed its “de minimis” import duty exemption on small packages, hitting its sales in the country.

The EU is also cracking down on the loophole – introducing a €3 (£2.56) duty on small parcels imported from outside the trading bloc in June – and intends to phase it out, while the UK has said it will do the same by October 2028.

Nevertheless, the company has still become one of the world’s biggest listed fashion groups, with a valuation around the same as the Swedish retailer H&M. The Zara owner, Inditex, has a market capitalisation of about $213bn.
after newsletter promotion
Shein moved its headquarters to Singapore at about the start of 2022, a move viewed by analysts as designed to avoid increasing scrutiny of Chinese companies.

Founded by the entrepreneur Chris Xu, the company runs most of its operations from China but sells all its goods outside the country. It reached a valuation of $100bn in an April 2022 fundraising round, making it the third most valuable startup in the world at the time.

After forced labour concerns were raised, Shein said it had tightened its supplier policies, enforced through regular audits, with any child or forced labour violations becoming grounds for immediate termination of contract.

articles.title: Nigeria rethinks criminalization of suicide
articles.summary: LAGOS — In Nigeria, surviving a suicide attempt can mean facing not only the trauma of the ordeal but also the threat of prosecution. Laws dating back decades, including some inherited from the…

blocks.text: LAGOS — In Nigeria, surviving a suicide attempt can mean facing not only the trauma of the ordeal but also the threat of prosecution.
Laws dating back decades, including some inherited from the colonial era, criminalize attempted suicide — and, advocates say, deter people in crisis from seeking the care they need.
The government now says those laws have run their course and must change.
Africa’s most populous country records about 300,000 suicide attempts annually, with at least 7,000 deaths, according to health minister Mohammed Ali Pate, citing World Health Organization figures.
“Suicide is a major public health concern in Nigeria,” Pate told journalists in August. “The idea is attempted suicide is not a crime.”
Criminalising suicide attempts discourages people from seeking urgent help, said Kingsley Okonoda, a professor of psychiatry at the University of Jos.
“So many people will not present for treatment or will not come out even after the attempted suicide has failed because of fear of being prosecuted,” Okonoda told AFP.
Limited access to treatment
Pate said the government would send a bill to the National Assembly to push forward with the decriminalization plan, with the aim of reducing suicide deaths and attempts by 15 percent by 2030.

Across Nigeria’s 36 states, suicide attempts typically carry a one-year prison term, though in Muslim-majority Jigawa, governed under sharia in parallel to the state and federal justice systems, the penalty can be as high as five years, according to Decriminalize Suicide Worldwide, an advocacy campaign.
Supporters of the reform are calling for the federal government to harmonize the law across the country — and also warn decriminalization alone may not be enough.
Less than 35 percent of Nigerians believe people in their communities can access help for mental or emotional problems, according to a 2024 report from Afrobarometer, a pollster.
Stigma remains a major barrier to treatment, with many Nigerians still viewing mental health problems as spiritual afflictions.

Nigeria also faces a severe shortage of qualified medical professionals, with fewer than 1,000 psychiatrists serving more than 200 million people, according to 2024 figures from the Association of Psychiatrists in Nigeria (APN).
“Decriminalizing suicide must be accompanied by a deliberate expansion of access to quality mental health services. Accessibility must be matched by affordability,” APN said in a statement to AFP.
Economic crisis, insecurity
Along with the proposed amendments, experts said the government must also address factors that predispose people to suicide.
Economic hardship, rising poverty, insecurity and social isolation are among the drivers of mental illness and suicidal behaviour, according to the APN.

The country has endured years of economic strain, with President Bola Tinubu’s major reforms blamed for pushing up the cost of living, even as the government says they are attracting international investment and creating macroeconomic stability.

Inflation reached a record high of 34 percent in mid-2024 before slowing to 15.4 percent in July. Poverty has continued to rise, affecting 63 percent of the population, according to the International Monetary Fund.

The country is also grappling with a 17-year jihadist insurgency in the northeast. Rampant kidnap-for-ransom attacks and farmer-herder violence wrack the north-central region, while secessionist agitation rumbles on in the southeast.

The government “has a crucial role to play beyond the health sector. Every meaningful intervention that makes life safer, more dignified and more economically viable is, in itself, a mental health intervention and suicide prevention,” APN said.
A suicide prevention bill submitted by several NGOs to the National Assembly in 2024, seeking to protect the “rights of persons with suicidal behaviour”, is yet to be passed.
Promoters said the bill would complement proposed amendments to the country’s existing mental health laws.
“The amendment and the National Suicide Prevention Bill are two halves of one reform,” said Taiwo Lateef Sheikh, of the Nigeria Suicide Prevention Advocacy Working Group.
“One removes the punishment, the other builds what should be there instead.” /dl
